name: Bajaj Finance Ltd
about: Bajaj Finance is mainly engaged in the business of lending. BFL has a diversified lending portfolio across retail, SME and commercial customers with a significant presence in urban and rural India. It also accepts public and corporate deposits and offers variety of financial services products to its customers.(Source : 202003 Annual Report Page No:124)

sections.one_liner: Deposit-taking consumer NBFC with ₹5.85 lakh cr AUM; growth now outruns capital, prompting a ₹17,500 cr raise.
business: Deposit-taking NBFC lending to retail, MSME and commercial customers via 4,098 locations, 2,571 of them rural. [AR FY26]
Segments: consumer durables, personal loans, MSME, wheels, gold, mortgages, microfinance and payments. Segment AUM shares not disclosed. [AR FY26]
Gold is the fastest-scaling book: ₹17,831 cr AUM and 1,314 branches in FY26, rising to ₹24,000+ cr and 2,022 branches by Q2. [AR FY26]
Consolidated figures include BHFL (86.70% held, down from 88.75%) and BFSL. Digital contributed 16.32% of business. [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27 (Sep-26): revenue ₹24,546 cr, +22.8% YoY. PAT ₹6,367 cr, +28.7%. OPM 36% vs 34% a year ago. [Numbers]
TTM revenue ₹90,330 cr, PAT ₹22,067 cr. OPM about 34%, including the Dec-25 quarter at 28%. [Numbers]
Valuation: P/E 26.9x, P/B about 4.8x (₹946 price vs ₹198 book), dividend yield 0.58%. [Numbers]
Reported ROE 18.2% and ROCE 10.9% trail the 20.6% quarterly ROE management cited. Price is 20% below its ₹1,178 high. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue compounding is steady: 5y CAGR 25.2%, 3y 25.6%, from ₹26,673 cr in FY21 to ₹81,985 cr in FY26. [Numbers]
Margin compression: 3y PAT CAGR of 18.9% lags 25.6% revenue growth. OPM fell from 39% (FY23) to 33% (FY26). [Numbers]
PAT growth slowed to 16.1% in FY25 and 15.2% in FY26, then re-accelerated to 27.6% and 28.7% in the last two quarters. [Numbers]
Revenue growth bottomed at 16.5% (Dec-25), down from 27.3% (Dec-24). It recovered to 22.8% by Sep-26. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Debt is not disclosed. Implied equity is about ₹1.23 lakh cr (₹198 book × ~623 cr shares), against AUM of ₹5.85 lakh cr: about 4.7x. [Numbers]
Deposit share slipped from 15% (₹68,500 cr) in Q1 to 14% in Q2. Cost of funds fell 9bp QoQ to 7.31%. [Q2FY27 call]
₹11,700 cr QIP plus ₹5,800 cr warrants is about 14% of book. Retained ROE of ~16-17% cannot fund 26.5% AUM growth. [Q2FY27 call]
cash_quality: CFO is negative every year, from -₹42,112 cr (FY23) to -₹65,790 cr (FY26). CFO/PAT of -4.08 means loan growth consumes all profit. [Numbers]
FY26 FCF was -₹66,686 cr against PAT of ₹19,332 cr. Roughly ₹3.4 of external funding was needed per ₹1 of profit. [Numbers]
Earnings quality rests on provisioning: ₹300 cr (Q1) and ₹337 cr (Q2) macro overlays, ₹512 cr overlay stock, and an LGD floor. [Q2FY27 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Diverge: the call claimed FY26 PAT +24%. Reported consolidated PAT grew 15.2% (₹16,779 cr to ₹19,332 cr). The gap is unexplained. [Q4FY26 call]
Diverge: Q4 'core' PAT was +26.7%, but reported Mar-26 PAT was +22.2%. Dec-25 PAT fell 5.6%, likely from the ₹1,406 cr accelerated ECL. [AR FY26]
Agree: profit is outgrowing the book. Q2 PAT rose 28.7% vs AUM 26.5%. Revenue at +22.8% lags AUM, consistent with NIM moderation. [Numbers]
Tension: management calls leverage manageable yet raises ₹17,500 cr, about 3% of ₹5.89 lakh cr market cap, while guiding 19-21% ROE. [Q2FY27 call]
guidance: FY27 AUM growth raised from 20-24% (Q4FY26) to 26-27% (Q2FY27). Medium-term 20-25% unchanged. [Q2FY27 call]
FY27 credit cost 145-160bp (Q4FY26). Q2 says FY27 is likely among the lowest credit-cost years in four. [Q2FY27 call]
FY27 ROA 4.4-4.6% and ROE 19-20%. Long-term: 20-25% profit growth at 19-21% ROE. [Q4FY26 call]
FY27 opex/NTI to improve 25-40bp from 33.8%. NIM to moderate 10-15bp. [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 customer additions raised from 15-17M to 18-20M. New loans 60-62M. Gold AUM ₹29,000-31,000 cr. About 2,800 gold branches. [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.delivered: H1 AUM +26.5% (call). Guidance raised to 26-27%. Q2 revenue +22.8%. Full year unreported.

ledger.promised: Profit growth to exceed balance-sheet growth [Q4FY26 call]
Credit cost trending down to 145-160bp for FY27 [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Loan loss 1.54% Q1, 1.56% Q2 (call). Not in NUMBERS. Full year pending.
Q2 ROE 20.6%, ROA 4.6% (call). Screener ROE 18.2%. QIP dilution ahead.

ledger.promised: Gold loans to cross ~5% of AUM by FY27 [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Gold 4.1% of balance sheet at Q2. Needs about 1pt more in H2.

ledger.promised: MSME back to growth momentum by Q3 [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Dec-26 not reported. Q2 call cites MSME GNPA deterioration from flat growth.
NIM not disclosed. Revenue +22.8% vs AUM +26.5% suggests some yield compression.
Q2 opex to total income 33% (different denominator). OPM 36% vs 34% YoY.

bull: Guidance raised mid-year: AUM from 20-24% to 26-27%, customers from 15-17M to 18-20M. H1 AUM already +26.5%. [Q2FY27 call]
Credit is improving: loan loss 1.56% vs 1.88% YoY, NNPA 42bp, with a ₹512 cr overlay buffer. [Q2FY27 call]
Operating leverage is returning: OPM 36% in Jun/Sep-26 vs 33% in FY26. PAT +28.7% against a 26.9x P/E. [Numbers]
bear: A ₹17,500 cr raise shows growth outrunning internal capital. Add ₹18,152 cr BHFL RPT limit and ~3% dilution. [Q2FY27 call]
Stress is building: gold Stage 2 +₹1,047 cr, monsoon at 87% of LPA, 2PL/3PL at 7% of origination, MSME GNPA rising. [Q2FY27 call]
Paying 4.8x book for 18.2% reported ROE. FY26 PAT grew only 15.2%, and Dec-25 PAT fell 5.6%. [Numbers]
questions: Reconcile claimed 24% FY26 PAT growth with reported 15.2% consolidated growth.
What FY28 ROE results after ₹17,500 cr dilution at 26-27% growth?
How much of the ₹1,047 cr gold Stage 2 rolled into Stage 3?
How much fee income is at risk if insurance commission norms tighten?

analyst_pushback.question: Why not offer short-term gold loans given easier LTV with shorter interest accrual?
analyst_pushback.response: Short tenure creates cumbersome customer experience requiring frequent rollover; inadvertently pushes customers into delinquency

analyst_pushback.question: Should low-credit-cost two-wheeler customers be included in cross-sell franchise?
analyst_pushback.response: Yes, segment remains unchanged; maintain open architecture targeting 30-35% credit cost; pool likely to be low

analyst_pushback.question: What is driving MSME GNPA deterioration and are there other stress areas?
analyst_pushback.response: Pure mathematics from flat growth; 3MOB/6MOB/9MOB metrics better than 2019 levels; no blind spots identified

analyst_pushback.question: Why raise capital now when leverage is manageable; why not dilute BHFL over time instead?
analyst_pushback.response: Raise smaller relative to doubled balance sheet growth; capital gives BHFL transition time to repivot business model strategically

annual_report.business: BFL is a deposit-taking NBFC-ICC offering diversified lending to retail, MSME, and commercial customers across urban and rural India through 4,098 locations. Revenue from interest income on loans, deposits, service fees, and payments.

segments.name: Consumer Lending
segments.comment: Electronics, furniture, two/three-wheelers; ₹115,161 crore disbursed FY2026

segments.name: Personal Loans
segments.comment: Unsecured lending with EMI card enablement; ₹21,500 crore digital

segments.name: MSME Lending
segments.comment: Secured and unsecured lending to micro, small, medium enterprises

segments.name: Wheels Financing
segments.comment: Auto and two-wheeler financing; dealer network 10,000+

segments.name: Gold Loans
segments.comment: Secured lending against gold; 1,314 branches; ₹17,831 crore AUM

segments.name: Mortgages
segments.comment: Housing finance; ₹1,300 crore digital disbursals; SBU established

segments.name: Payments
segments.comment: UPI, wallet, FASTag, bill pay; 129.29 crore transactions

segments.name: Deposits
segments.comment: Public and corporate deposits; ₹497 crore digital mobilized

annual_report.revenue_mix: Digital contributed 16.32% of business. 4,098 locations span urban-rural (2,571 rural). Retail, MSME, commercial customer segments. Secured and unsecured lending diversified.
strategy: Customer-centric transformation using design thinking and propensity-led engagement
AI and data leadership: unstructured data, feature stores, vector databases, knowledge graphs
Lowest-risk positioning via AI-enabled fraud, compliance, risk, operations controls
Omnichannel expansion: 87M app users, 611M web visits, 4,098 locations
Product innovation: wealth management, solar financing, corporate leasing, NCMC distribution
annual_report.outlook: FY2030 targets: 200-220M customers, 19-21% ROE, 12-15% AI productivity gains, 50% operations cost reduction by FY2030. Strong FY2027 momentum. Management optimistic.
annual_report.capex_plans: Expand locations to 4,600-4,900 by FY2030. Gold branches scaled 964 to 1,314. Significant AI, data infrastructure and digital platform investments. Specific amounts not disclosed.
risks: Geopolitical escalation (Middle East, Iran) impacting commodity prices and trade flows
US-China trade tensions, tariffs, semiconductor export control on strategic sectors
Global economic slowdown from elevated policy uncertainty and fragmentation
Commodity price volatility and supply chain disruptions
annual_report.flags: Material RPT with BHFL: ₹18,152 crore limit. BFL shareholding reduced 88.75% to 86.70%; ₹1,416 crore gain realized. Accelerated ECL provision ₹1,406 crore; LGD floor implemented.
